chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A woman from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he was in the house of Hafsa. The woman was dressed up and combed her hair. She entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! A woman does not propose to a husband, and I am a widow who has had no husband for a long time and has no children. Is there any need for you? If so, I have gifted myself to you, if you accept me.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spoke well to her and supplicated for her, then he said: 'O sister of the Ansar, may Allah recompense you with goodness from the Messenger of Allah, for your men have helped me, and your women have desired me.'

Hafsa said to her: 'How little is your modesty, and how audacious and covetous of men you are!' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Restrain yourself from her, O Hafsa, for she is better than you; she desired the Messenger of Allah, but you blamed her and faulted her.'

Then he said to the woman: 'Go, may Allah have mercy on you, for Allah has obligated Paradise for you due to your desire for me and your presenting yourself for my love and delight. My command will come to you, if Allah wills.'
And a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet desires to marry her — exclusively for you, and not for the other believers.
Thus, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted the woman gifting herself to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and that is not permissible for anyone else.

key_terms.أَيِّمٌ: A widow or divorcee who is not currently married

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman gifting herself to the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific legal privilege (khaṣṣiyya) of the Prophet Muhammad, where a woman could directly offer herself in marriage without a formal proposal, a right exclusive to him as indicated by the phrase 'khāliṣatan laka' in Quran 33:50. The event underscores the virtue of the Ansar women and serves as a basis for the juristic distinction between the Prophet's unique marital permissions and those of the general community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A woman from the Helpers came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>as</sup> was in the house of Hafsa, and the woman had dressed up and combed her hair. So she came to Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> and said, ‘O Rsool-Allah<sup>asws</sup>! The women do not tend to propose to the husband, and I am a woman who is widowed and have not married since a long time, and do not have children. So is there a need for you<sup>asws</sup>, for if there is, so I have gifted myself to you<sup>asws</sup>, if you accept me’.

So Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said good things to her and supplicated for her, then said: ‘O sister of the Helpers. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Recompnse you with goodness from Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for your men have helped me<sup>asws</sup>, and your womenfolk have desired me<sup>asws</sup>’.

So Hafsa said to her, ‘How little is your shame, and how audacious of you and your coveting the men!’ So Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said to her: ‘Restrain from her, O Hafsa, for she is better than you in desiring Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup>, but you are blaming her and faulting her’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to the woman of the Helpers: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Obligated the Paradise for you due to your desire for me and your being pleased with my<sup>asws</sup> love and my delight. My<sup>asws</sup> order will come to you, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
Thus, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Revealed [33:50] and a believing woman if she gave herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet desired to marry her - specially for you, apart from Believers.
He<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Thus, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Permitted the woman gifting herself to Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup>, and that is not Permissible for others’.
en.sarwar: 53. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a woman of al-Ansar (people of al-Madinah) came to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. She came in the house of Hafsah and she was well dressed and groomed. She came to the Messenger of Allah and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, women do not propose for marriage to men. I am unmarried since a long time and I have no children. Are you interested in me? If you are interested I give myself to you as gift if you accept me.’

The Messenger of Allah prayed for her and admired. He (the Messenger of Allah) then said, ‘O sister (in belief) from al-Ansar (people of al- Madinah), may Allah on behalf of His Messenger grant you good recompense. Your men supported me and your women showed interest in me.’

Hafsah then said, ‘How shameless of you and being audacious, and craving for men.’ The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said to her, ‘Leave her alone, O Hafsah, she is better than you. She has shown interest in the Messenger of Allah and you blame her and consider it a fault.’

He (the Imam) said that he (the Messenger of Allah) said to the woman, ‘You may leave, Allah has granted you kindness and has made paradise obligatory for you because of your showing interest in me and that you love me and want to make me happy. My command will soon come by the will of Allah.

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, then revealed this, ‘. . . if a believing woman gifts herself to the prophet and if the prophet wants to marry her then she is for him only and not for the believing men.’ [33:49]

He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, made gifting of a woman herself to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, lawful and it is not lawful for people other than him (the Messenger of Allah).”’
